title: E-Stop Recovery
description: Guide through safe E-stop reset and recovery sequence

n1.text: First things first — is the area around the machine clear and safe? No one near moving parts, nothing jammed in the mechanism?
n1.hint: Walk the perimeter before we touch anything.

options.label: No, there's a hazard
options.transition: Stop right there. Don't reset anything yet.

n2.text: Alright, go ahead and twist the E-stop mushroom button to release it. Some units need a quarter-turn clockwise. Did it pop back out?
n2.hint: The button should spring back to its raised position when released properly.

options.label: Yes, it released
options.transition: Good, the E-stop circuit should be clearing now.

options.label: No, it's stuck
options.transition: That's unusual — the button mechanism might be damaged.

n3.text: Now check the PLC — is the E-stop fault cleared on the HMI or fault indicator? Some systems need a separate fault reset button after releasing the E-stop.
n3.hint: Look for a blue or green 'Reset' pushbutton near the HMI, or a reset option on screen.

options.label: No, still showing fault
options.transition: The safety circuit hasn't fully cleared yet. Let's reset it.

n_ok.text: E-stop is recovered and the system is ready to restart. Before you hit start, do a quick visual check that everything looks right.
steps: Verify all guards and doors are closed
Confirm no one is in the hazard zone
Press the Start button to resume operation
Watch the first cycle to make sure everything runs clean

n_hazard.text: Do NOT reset the E-stop until the hazard is cleared. This is a safety issue.
steps: Clear the hazard — remove jammed material, move personnel clear
If there's equipment damage, lock out and tag out before investigating
Once the area is safe, come back and we'll walk through the reset

n_stuck.text: The E-stop button mechanism is stuck or damaged. Don't force it — you could break the contact block.
steps: Lock out and tag out the machine at the main disconnect
Inspect the E-stop button assembly for damage or debris
Replace the E-stop unit if the mechanism is broken
Test the new E-stop before returning to service

n_reset.text: The safety circuit needs a manual fault reset. This is normal — it's a two-step process to prevent accidental restarts.
steps: Find the fault reset button (usually blue, near the HMI or main panel)
Verify the E-stop indicator clears on the HMI
If it still won't clear, power-cycle the safety relay module
